0.title: Stage 0: Tutorial - First Circuit
0.desc: Recreate the basic circuit by following the instructed logic path. Invert input IN1, combine it with IN2 using AND, and output to OUT1.

1.title: Stage 1: NOT Gate
1.desc: Build a circuit that inverts the input signal. 0 must output 1, and 1 must output 0.

2.title: Stage 2: OR Gate
2.desc: Design logic that outputs 1 when at least one of the two inputs is 1.

3.title: Stage 3: AND Gate
3.desc: Build a circuit that outputs 1 only when both inputs are 1.

4.title: Stage 4: NOR Gate
4.desc: Implement logic that inverts the result of an OR operation.

5.title: Stage 5: NAND Gate
5.desc: Design a circuit that inverts the result of an AND operation.

6.title: Stage 6: XOR Gate
6.desc: Reconstruct a circuit that outputs 1 only when the two inputs are different.

7.title: Stage 7: Majority Gate
7.desc: Output 1 only when at least two of the three inputs are 1.

8.title: Stage 8: Parity Checker
8.desc: Build a circuit that outputs 1 only when the number of 1s is odd.

9.title: Stage 9: Half Adder
9.desc: Compute the sum of two 1-bit inputs and output Sum (S) and Carry (C) separately.

10.title: Stage 10: Full Adder
10.desc: Design a circuit that adds three 1-bit inputs and outputs Sum (S) and Carry (C).

11.title: Stage 11: 2-to-4 Decoder
11.desc: Configure the circuit so that exactly one of four outputs becomes 1 for each 2-bit input combination.

12.title: Stage 12: 4-to-1 MUX
12.desc: Pass one of four inputs directly to OUT according to select signals (S1 S0).

13.title: Stage 13: 2-bit Comparator
13.desc: Compare 2-bit numbers A and B so that only one of A>B, A=B, or A<B is 1.

14.title: Stage 14: 2-bit Adder
14.desc: Add 2-bit numbers A and B and output the 3-bit result (S2 S1 S0).

15.title: Stage 15: mod 4 2-bit Subtractor
15.desc: Compute A − B for two 2-bit numbers using mod 4 arithmetic and output the 2-bit result.

16.title: Stage 16: 2-bit Max Selector
16.desc: Output the larger value between two 2-bit numbers A and B.

17.title: Stage 17: 2-bit Multiplier
17.desc: Compute the product of two 2-bit numbers and output the 4-bit result (P3 P2 P1 P0).

18.title: Stage 18: Mod 3 Remainder
18.desc: Output the remainder of dividing 4-bit input A by 3 as a 2-bit value (R1 R0).

19.title: Crossroad
19.desc: Design paths so two input signals are delivered to their own outputs accurately without interference.

20.title: Fixed XOR
20.desc: Implement XOR behavior exactly within the fixed input and output structure.

21.title: 3-bit Shifter
21.desc:
Design a circuit that cyclically shifts three signals based on control signal IN4.
IN4 = 0 -> output as-is
IN4 = 1 -> rotate by one position

22.title: Fixed 2-to-4 Decoder
22.desc: Configure the circuit so exactly one output is activated for each input combination.

23.title: Priority Gate
23.desc: Select and output only the single 1 with the highest priority among multiple inputs.

24.title: 2's complement
24.desc: Design a circuit that computes the 2's complement of a 4-bit binary number.

25.title: Storage Switch
25.desc: Store DATA in VALUE when LOAD is on. Otherwise keep the saved value, even if DATA changes. VALUE starts at 0.

26.title: Toggle Light
26.desc: Invert LIGHT on every tick with PRESS=1; otherwise hold it. Presses on consecutive ticks each toggle the light. Initially LIGHT=0. Observe outputs after each tick.

27.title: 2-to-1 Selector
27.desc: Build a combinational selector: OUT=A when SEL=0, otherwise OUT=B. No memory is needed.

28.title: Fault Indicator
28.desc: FAULT turns ALARM on and keeps it on. ACK clears it, but FAULT wins if both arrive together. With no request, hold the value. ALARM starts off.

29.title: Response Check
29.desc: Check responses from both paths A and B. Remember the first response for as long as it takes the other to arrive. Set GO to 1 on the tick when both have arrived, then clear both records. Repeated responses from one path count only once. Simultaneous responses also count, and new responses can be received from the very next tick. If A and B arrive together every tick, GO stays 1 on those consecutive ticks. Otherwise, GO is 0 on ticks without a complete pair. Initially there are no records and GO is 0.

30.title: Automatic Door
30.desc: OPEN keeps DOOR on for three ticks, including the request tick. Another request restarts the timer. OPEN 1→0→0→0 should produce DOOR 1→1→1→0. The door starts closed.

31.title: Rising Edge Detector
31.desc: Turn on RISE for the tick when SIGNAL changes from 0 to 1. Holding SIGNAL on must not trigger it again. Treat SIGNAL before the first tick as 0.

32.title: Up/Down Counter
32.desc: Count from 0 to 3 using BIT1·BIT0. INC alone adds one; DEC alone subtracts one. Wrap between 3 and 0. Both on or both off leave the count unchanged. Start at 0; RESET overrides both requests and clears the count.

33.title: Four Brightness Levels
33.desc: Use DUTY1·DUTY0 to select brightness 0–3. A phase starts at 0 and advances through 1→2→3→0 each tick. Turn PWM on when the phase is below DUTY, giving 0%, 25%, 50% or 75% brightness. RESET returns the phase to 0; the same lighting rule still applies.

34.title: Watchdog
34.desc: Turn TIMEOUT on after three consecutive ticks without KICK and keep it on. KICK immediately clears TIMEOUT and restarts the wait. TIMEOUT starts off.

35.title: Bouncing Button
35.desc: Change CLEAN only when RAW has stayed the same for three ticks, on the third tick. Ignore shorter glitches in either direction. CLEAN and the previous samples start at 0.

36.title: Fair Access
36.desc: Grant A_OK or B_OK to the side requesting access. If both request, choose the opposite of the last winner; the first tie goes to A. Single grants also update the turn. With no request, turn both outputs off and remember the turn.

37.title: ABBA Lock
37.desc: SIGNAL means A when 1 and B when 0. Accept a letter only when SUBMIT is on. Turn UNLOCKED on when the latest four submitted letters are ABBA, including within AABBA. Waiting preserves the letters; once unlocked, stay unlocked. Start with no letters.

38.title: Addressed Storage
38.desc: Build two two-bit storage slots, both starting at 00. WRITE saves D1·D0 to the slot selected by ADDR. Q1·Q0 always reads the selected slot: changing ADDR changes the readout immediately, and a write tick shows the new value.

39.title: Undo Once
39.desc: SAVE stores D1·D0 and keeps the previous value for one UNDO. Undoing clears UNDO_AVAILABLE until the next SAVE. Even saving the same value enables undo. SAVE wins when both are requested. Current and previous values start at 00, with undo unavailable.

40.title: Mailbox
40.desc:
SEND puts DATA into a one-bit mailbox; TAKE retrieves it into DATA_OUT. Pulse ACCEPTED for a successful send and VALID for a successful take.
Together, take first, then send. If empty, only send; if full without a take, reject the send. Hold DATA_OUT unless a take succeeds. FULL shows the resulting state. Start empty with all outputs at 0.

41.title: Last In, First Out
41.desc:
PUSH stores DATA in a stack of up to two bits. POP retrieves the newest bit into DATA_OUT and pulses VALID. Otherwise hold DATA_OUT and clear VALID.
Together, pop first, then push. If empty, only push; if full without a pop, ignore the push. EMPTY and FULL show the resulting state. Start empty with DATA_OUT and VALID at 0.

42.title: First In, First Out
42.desc:
PUSH stores DATA in a queue of up to two bits. POP retrieves the oldest bit into DATA_OUT and pulses VALID. Otherwise hold DATA_OUT and clear VALID.
Together, pop first, then push. If empty, only push; if full without a pop, ignore the push. EMPTY and FULL show the resulting state. Start empty with DATA_OUT and VALID at 0.

43.title: Serial Receiver
43.desc: Accept one DATA bit whenever RECEIVE is on, highest bit first. On the fourth bit, update Q3·Q2·Q1·Q0 together and pulse DONE for that tick. Otherwise hold Q and clear DONE. Waiting preserves progress; each four bits forms a new word. Q starts at 0000.

44.title: Serial Transmitter
44.desc:
While idle, START captures D3·D2·D1·D0. Send D3 immediately, then D2, D1 and D0 on the next three ticks. Ignore input changes and START through the last bit; a new word can start on the following tick.
VALID is on for each bit; BUSY is on while more bits remain. The last bit has VALID=1, BUSY=0. Idle holds SERIAL and clears both flags. RESET overrides START, cancels transmission and clears all outputs. All outputs start at 0.

45.title: Accumulator
45.desc: When ADD is on, add D1·D0 to Q1·Q0. Wrap the two-bit sum after 3. Otherwise hold the sum. Start at 0; RESET overrides ADD and clears the sum.

46.title: Divide Over Time
46.desc:
Divide A (0–7) by B (1–3) to produce quotient Q and remainder R. Inputs stay fixed during each calculation; bit 0 is the lowest bit.
Turn on COMPLETE when ready. Q and R must be correct at the first completion on ticks 1–10. Earlier values do not matter; missing the deadline fails. Each calculation starts with all memory at 0.

hints.content: Outputs true only when A∨B is true but A∧B is false.
A XOR B = (A∨B)∧¬(A∧B) = (A∧¬B)∨(¬A∧B)
Outputs true only when A and B, B and C, or C and A are true.
The XOR operation works like addition mod 2.
(A XOR B) XOR C
Determine what operations OUT1 and OUT2 perform on IN1 and IN2.
OUT1 = A XOR B, OUT2 = A∧B
Determine what operations OUT1 and OUT2 perform on IN1, IN2, and IN3.
OUT1 = (A∧B)∨(B∧C)∨(C∧A), OUT2 = (A XOR B) XOR C
Try building circuits for A∧B, A∨B, and C instead of A, B, and C.
Combine circuits for OUT1, OUT2, OUT3, and OUT4 into one.
OUT1, OUT2, OUT3, and OUT4 can be expressed as AND operations of IN1, IN2, ¬IN1, and ¬IN2.
Use ternary operations.
Process S1 and S0 sequentially.
Treat (A,B,S) as a ternary operator: ((IN1,IN2,S0),(IN3,IN4,S0),S1)
Connect DATA to D and LOAD to EN.
Feed NOT Q back into D, and enable storage with PRESS.
Enable the two paths with SEL and NOT SEL, then combine them with OR.
Store FAULT with EN=FAULT OR ACK.
Remember which paths have responded. Make sure responses used for one check cannot be reused for the next.
Remember three OPEN samples with D blocks and combine them using two binary OR gates.
Store the previous SIGNAL and the detected edge in separate D blocks. Compute the edge using the old previous value.
Remember one, two and three-or-more silent ticks with D blocks. KICK clears the chain.
Remember two previous RAW samples and CLEAN. Set on three ones, clear on three zeros, otherwise hold.
Determine when each bit toggles. Use NOT(Q) as DATA and a bit-specific EN; RESET must clear both bits.
Use two state bits for four phases. A Gray-code cycle can simplify the next-state logic; compare its phase with DUTY.
Remember the last winner with EN=request present, and register whether this tick had any request.
Shift submitted letters using SUBMIT as EN. Detect the previous A,B,B and the new A; retain the unlocked state.
Derive the toggle condition for each bit, including carry. Use enabled memories and give RESET priority.
Give each word its own write enable, then select the addressed word for reading.
Keep current and backup words plus an availability bit. SAVE must copy the old current value into the backup.
Keep received bits and a four-step progress state. Publish all four bits together and register DONE for exactly the completion tick.
Store the captured word and transmission progress. Register SERIAL and VALID, and derive BUSY from the remaining work.
Track two data slots and occupancy. Preserve the last popped value independently of the current top, and register POP success.
Track the head, tail and occupancy. A POP exposes the oldest item and shifts any remaining item toward the head. Keep the last popped value separately.
Keep payload, occupancy and last delivered data separately. Process a successful TAKE before deciding whether SEND can be accepted.
You can count units while accumulating quotient and remainder, then assert COMPLETE. The example solution finishes in A+1 ticks, but ANY correct first completion within 10 ticks is accepted.
